advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Emit a `container_ps_ok`/join heartbeat (or fold ps-failure into a distinct signal) so a failed `docker ps` label join is not silently reported as a healthy census of all-`unlabeled` containers.
evidence: `container_ps=$(timeout 15 docker ps --no-trunc ... 2>/dev/null) || true` — the ps result is never tested for success or non-emptiness

awk PS branch `service[$2] = ($3 != "") ? $3 : $4` builds an empty map when container_ps is empty, so ST rows resolve `(service[$2] != "" ? service[$2] : "unlabeled")` to `unlabeled` for all containers
container_stats_ok is set to 1 off any ROW (line 375), which fires as long as `docker stats` alone succeeds — independent of whether the ps join ran
ABSENCE: no ps_ok / join-heartbeat metric exists and test_a_failed_container_census_publishes_its_heartbeat only covers the stats-fails case, not stats-succeeds-but-ps-fails
advisory.finding: In observability.sh's §2d census, `docker ps` (the name->service label join) has no liveness check: if it fails or times out while `docker stats` succeeds, the awk service map is empty and EVERY container's dimension silently falls back to `service=unlabeled`, yet `container_stats_ok` still publishes 1. A failed label join — the exact instrument this redesign exists to make trustworthy — is indistinguishable from every container genuinely lacking both labels.
scenarios: docker daemon under memory pressure answers `docker stats` but `docker ps` times out at 15s
the exact loaded-box condition this metric exists to catch degrades the label join first

advisory.finding: The 'instrumentation must never fail the run it measures' contract is untested at the actual seam: no test drives the gate_peak_rss context manager (the wrapper installed at both entry points) with a raising peak_rss_bytes()/resource.getrusage(). gate_peak_rss calls peak_rss_bytes() unguarded at line 99 (before yield) and line 103 (in finally), and the sibling test test_measurement_failure_never_breaks_the_gate proves peak_rss_bytes() re-raises OSError — so an OSError from getrusage would abort the gate or mask its exception, and no test would catch it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm `docker ps {{.Names}}` and `docker stats {{.Name}}` produce identical join keys for all containers on the box (single-name only), or normalize the ps key to the primary name.
advisory.finding: The name->service join keys `docker ps --format '{{.Names}}'` against `docker stats --format '{{.Name}}'`; `.Names` can be a comma-joined list while `.Name` is singular, so a container with more than one name would fail the join and be bucketed as `service=unlabeled` rather than under its real service identity.
